summary: A real, legally mandated job (annual homeschool portfolio evaluation), but the research found zero first-hand evidence that evaluators want software or lose meaningful time to this. The buyer pool is small, reachable only by outbound outreach, and the data is children's work.

demand.evidence: RESEARCH.md says outright: no first-hand evaluator complaints and no hours-per-family figures. Parent-side portfolio pain (ourjourneywestward.com, homeschoolgiveaways.com) is real but the parent is not the buyer. Nobody has asked for this, paid, or been upset by its absence.

statusQuo.evidence: Evaluators likely use Google Docs, email and templates at $0 (RESEARCH.md competitor table). Fees of $30-$150 per child (homeschoolfox.com, soft vendor figures) show the job is paid, but the workaround costs little. Parents already pay HomeschoolFox $12/mo and it already generates evaluator letters.

specificity.evidence: The buyer is a precise role (certified-teacher evaluator in PA/FL, 20+ families, listed in CHAP/FPEA directories), more specific than most ideas. But no named person, no heard consequence, and nothing at stake: it is side income, so a $19/mo tool is a hard sell.

wedge.evidence: Narrowest wedge is the PA/FL certification letter plus sorted portfolio PDF from pasted details. Buildable in a weekend, but a letter template filler is copyable from a Google Doc, so willingness to pay for the wedge is doubtful. The real value (draft narrative, intake link) sits in M2-M3.

futureFit.evidence: Generic LLMs let any evaluator draft narratives themselves; HomeschoolFox can add an evaluator view cheaply. The pool of paid evaluators per state is hundreds to low thousands and could shift with law changes.

premises: Evaluators spend meaningful time per family on assembling and writing, enough to pay for software. Not supported: no hours measured, no evaluator voices found.
Evaluators, not parents, are the right buyer. Plausible, but they are small independent operators on $30-$150 fees.
AI-drafted narratives are acceptable to evaluators and districts. Unverified; the evaluator attests and signs.
HomeschoolFox won't close the gap. Weak: it already makes evaluator letters and owns the family relationship.
Evaluators are reachable via CHAP/FPEA directories. Plausible but one-by-one outbound work, against near-zero overhead.
alternatives: Minimal (S): a free static PA/FL certification-letter generator plus portfolio index PDF, posted in evaluator and homeschool support groups, to see whether anyone uses it.
Lateral (S): sell parent-side or partner with HomeschoolFox/support groups, avoiding an outbound sales motion.
Ideal (M-L): full evaluator workspace with upload links, inbox, AI drafts and retention jobs (the PRD). Child-data liability; premature before demand is proven.
No overlapping repo of David's to extend.
wedge: A PA/FL certification letter and sorted-portfolio index generator for a single evaluator, tested by getting 5 evaluators to run it on a real family.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby, pure functions buildPortfolio and renderCertification, Vitest; $0. Proving test: renderCertification('PA', ...) contains child, district, school year and the appropriate-education sentence, and FL omits PA wording. Passing proves the code works, not that anyone wants it.

risks: No evidence of evaluator demand; the case is inferred.
HomeschoolFox or a plain ChatGPT workflow substitutes cheaply.
Children's work samples: privacy and deletion obligations, and a trust barrier for an unknown solo vendor.
Outbound-only acquisition conflicts with near-zero overhead.
killCriteria: Drop if, after contacting 15 evaluators, fewer than 3 say they spend over 30 minutes per family on writing and assembly, or fewer than 5 agree to try it on a real family, or no one converts to a $19/mo trial.
